title: Round 5 / ECDLP-13: prime-field factor-base frontier — literature and alternative factor-base definitions
question: What exactly is proven/conjectured about index calculus on E(F_p), p prime (Semaev 2004, Petit–Kosters–Messeng 2016, Amadori–Pintore–Sala, Huang–Kosters–Yeo, Diem, Galbraith–Gaudry survey), and are there algebraically defined factor bases on prime fields other than small-x (e.g. x in a multiplicative subgroup, images of small-degree maps/isogenies, points with small-height lifts) whose relation yield or decomposition cost can be tested cheaply at toy sizes?

sources.title: Semaev, Summation polynomials and the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves (ePrint 2004/031)
Petit, Kosters, Messeng, Algebraic approaches for the ECDLP over prime fields (PKC 2016)
Amadori, Pintore, Sala, On the discrete logarithm problem for prime-field elliptic curves (ePrint 2017/609)
Galbraith, Gaudry, Recent progress on the ECDLP (ePrint 2015/1022)
Kosters, Yeo, Notes on summation polynomials (arXiv 1503.08001)
Diem, On the discrete logarithm problem in elliptic curves (Compositio 2011)
Hu, Implementation analysis of index calculus method on elliptic curves over prime finite fields (ePrint 2024/1923, unrefereed)

claims: Literature (verified at abstract level; PKM full text read): no proven or established sub-sqrt(p) prime-field ECDLP index calculus; PKM 2016 factor bases (coset of smooth-order subgroup of F_p^*, or isogeny-coset on auxiliary curve) are already the 'x in multiplicative subgroup' proposal; complexity open (Groebner step not analysable).

Experimental (toy, m=2, p<=2^18, 24 curves, seed 20261103): sum-set coverage and additive energy of x in aH, x=t^2, x=1/t equal those of small-x and random sets of equal size within ~1% at 2^18; no coset concentration of sums.
Experimental: scanning decomposition of random R costs ~34 n field multiplications at 2^18 (linear in n=|V|); no sub-scan decomposition method found; this does not prove none exists.
next_action: PI: decide whether to run a PKM-style resultant/Groebner experiment (m=3, smooth h, p~2^20) measuring T and a Coppersmith-style small-root test for F3; review literature claims marked unverified (HKY content, Momonari-Kudo, McGuire-Mueller).
